TO TILE BURGESSES Or THE NORTH-EAST WARD. LaTifigs and GEtrrtxxEls,—My 'term of office in the Town Comibk expires at the end of this month, and I offer myself for re-election. M•y views on the working of the Sanitary Committee and the Gas Committee have been so often expressed during the ixolt seven or eight years, that 1 do not think it necessary in this 'address to do more than $ll this way refer to them. If the votes that I have recorded in the past meet with your tippraval, I hope you will show the same by giving your .suffrages in my favour, and 'placing me and my colleague, as Candidates of the Ratepayers' Association, at the head of the poll. . I remain, Ladies and Gentlemen, tlour Obedient Servant, FRANCIS DIXON, Warrington, October nth, 1988.

TO THE BURGESSES OF THE NORTH-EAST WARD. LADIES AND GENTLEAOOI,—Having received a unanimous invitation from the Ratepayers' Association to become atrandi- date for the representation of your. Ward in the 'Town Council, I have much pleasure in placing my services at your disposal. As a Member of The Ratepayers' Association, I shall con- sider it my duty, at all times, to devote my best attention to your interests, by proposing and supporting a policy ofeconomy combined with efficiency. I know, and regret to know, that complaints are very numerous about the serious nuisance caused br—tbe Inter- cepting Depert in Lyth,goe's-lane, and if elected mill endea- vour, by all the means at my command, to influence the Council to make ra most searching inquiry with the view of having the evil remedied. The rates of the Borough are excessively high, standing, as they do, second In height on the list of Lancashire towns. Considering the 'increasing growth of Warniagton, we have a rightto expect and demand a substantial redaction.' I am of opinion that the price charged for gas is exorbi- tant. This has the effect of preventing many 'of the working clan from becoming consumers, thus plaelnglhem at a great disadvantage. If the price of gas were lowered, the consump- tion—and as a natural consequence the profits to the Borough —would be greMly increased. The momerthus gained could be advantageously spent in reducing the mtes, which would mean reducing rents. These and other kindred matters shall, if I am elected, receive at all times my best attention. Soliciting lour interest and votes, I am, your obedient migrant, , HENRY THORNTON. Warrington, October 19th, 1888.

My sole object shall be, without dictation or eliquism, to ensure the thoroughly good and Economical Government of • my native town; and, if, returned 'as your represemative, •will claim., utmost to secure your approbation. 'Ladies:4l.nd Gentlemen. in conclusion I may say that a shall not canvass nor ask for a vote from any one of you. I thillik; in these days of enlightenment and intelligence, to do so would,be absurd and degrading. ; I am free and indepen- dent of way Association. rING THE BURGESSES OF THE NORTH-EAST WARD. LADIES AND ,GENTLEMEN,—A requisition, numerously and influentially signed, asking me to stand as a Candidate to represent you in the Town Council, has been laid before me. After careful consideration, I have decided on seeking your suffrages. No word of reproach as to the Gentlemen who are my opponents will fall from my lips. If you think they are better qualified for the position than myself, by all means support them; if not, I shall esteem it an honour to represent you. You are the judges I Should you think fit to elect me, my desire is to enter the Council unfettered by political or other bias. My endeavour would be to secure Economy and Efficiency in the administration sof municipal affairs. The efforts which are being made by all creeds to improve the educational and social status of the community will receive my heartiest support, and, so far as I can afford, say practical sympathy. • . •The interests of -the industrial classes in a cemmunity like ours demand our;earuest attention. To those interests it will be my h:ghest pure to apply myself; at the same time the interests of the Capitalist and the Employer -of Labour are also entitled to our watchful care and consideration. If you elect srfe to represent your interests in the Council of our good eld Town. I can only hope that ray efforts may ; tend to promote Economy, Efficiency, and Prosperity. Soliciting your vote and interest, • remain, your obedient Servant, W. II- J. JENKINS. I Bank Ckaimb era, 1, Winwick-street, • Warrington, 17th October, 1888.

TO IPELE BURGESSES OF TLE LATCHFORD WARD. Wks and Gentlemen,—l have had tbe honour to represent your interests for the above Ward in the Town Council for about ten years, and am now a member of no less Glands's Committees, but am certainly not a member of the Sanitary Committee, and therefore have not voted for all the "extra- vagances and expensive experiments of the Longford Depart- ment, and in that way helped to spend thousands of pounds of your-money." which have been spent by that department, as alleged by my opponent, Mr. IL. J. Longton. 1 Without following Mr. Longton's address, and dealing ! separately with the theories and allegationt he sets forth in Iproof of my unfitness to cenainne as your representative in our local parliament, and of his prveminently high qualifica- tions for that honourable position. I will content nxyself by saying, diat in all I have doneas a member of the Council, I have been influenced only by a desire to do my duty conscien- tiously in all that concerns your interests and my own, for they are identical. If I vote in favour of ext t and unnecessary expenditure, as alleged, do I not punish myself as well as you P Have I net to bear my share of it.? Apply- ling the principles of common sense, is it at all likely that I should be a party to such an insane policy? I feel sure you vill not be misled by such false statements as have been put forth to defeat my re-election. .I therefore beg with great respect to solicit a renewal of your confidence on the Ist of November next, assuring you that in "the event of your so honouring me, I will spare no effort to show you how jealously I shall watch the expenditure, and *how earnestly I shall render all the assistance I can to secure the efficient and economical government of the -town in all its departments. If, on the otherhand, you should be of opinion that Mr. Longton could more diligently and ably represent you than I could, I shall cheerfully accept your decision, and retire, gratefully acknowledging your kindness for past favours. I have the honour to remain, Ladies and Gentlemen,-your faithful servant, JOSEPH TAYLOR. LATCHFORD, 17th October, 1888.

MUNICIPAL BLROIIIONS.—WARRINGTON, 1888. TO THE BURGESSES OF TILE •SOUTH-WEST WARD. LADIES AND GENTLEICEIC.-At the solicitation of an Influen- tial section of your number, we have expressed our readiness to become candidates forthe two vacancies it is your privi- lege to fill up in the Town %Council. Opposed ft us is one gentleman who is the nominee of the local Ratepayers' Association, the help of which latter in its present constituted form, .we, in common with the large majority of you, think we can very sensibly dispense with. The opinionin the ward is general, too, that we have plenty of good men amongst ourselves, able and willing to take the position of your representatives in the Town Council, with- out calling in assistance of doubtful value from helpers out- side. One of us has had the hoiCiiiiiiialready representlrtryou In the Council, and he hopes you will confer upon him the privilege of re-election. The other of us, if elected by the favour -of your votes, will appear there for the first time. But ques- rtions of any moment, whether now pending in the Council Chamber or done with, that have from time to time had con- sideration there, have hadhis observant attention, and he will not be unprepared, if elected, to take part in all important •:questions that have to come under discussion. We ask you to do us the favour of electing us, but hesitate to make 7..0 any specific promises of what you may expect -from us if you send us tothe Council. You have many good ,and able men in the .Couneil, and the desire of the whole of its members is, we are all ready to believe; to do the beet -they can for their townsmen as a body. If we promise you, MI we do, that we will apply all our ability, and endeavour to side with the ablest and best intentioned amongst them, you r will, we trust, consider this promises sufficient pledge for the confidence we venture :to dope you will extend to us. We have the honour to be, Your obedient Servants, NDWARD GREENALL, JUN, LEWIS VOISEY. WARRINGTON, 19th October, 1888.

THE CANOED/TRY MURDER.—Ry GISHIIie was charged, on remand, at Clerkenwell Police Court, on Friday; with the murder of Mrs. Wright, at Canonbury, in May last. He was committed for trial. Richard Ford, 4, South-st.. Farrtworth, committed suicide on Friday morning by lyinr, on a kitchen table and immersing his head in a bread mug full of water. He had recently been out of work. THE LONBON MURDERS.—The London police believe the Whitechapel kidney story to be a hoax. The city medical officer on Friday stated that the kidney could not have come from the body of the woman Eddowes. ELECTION INTELLIGENCE.—"DeWBbUry.—Mr. Mark Old- royd on Friday consented to contest Dewsbury as the Gladstonian candidate, provided the Liberals generally supported him.—Merthyr Tydvil.—The writ for the election of a member of Parliament for Merthyr Tydvil. in the room of the late Mr. Henry Richard, was received on Friday. The nomination is fixed for Tues- day next, and the polling for the following Friday. ANOTHER ALARMING FIRE IN LONDON.—The premises of a confectioner and tobacconist, in Old Kent-road, London, were destroyed by fire early on Friday morning. All the inmates are reported to have reached the street in safety; but a young man was rescued by the local fire brigade in a half conscious condition. Two of the firemen were blown from the escape by an explosion of gas in the street, and one of them was conveyed to Guy's Hospital, having been seriously injured. THE CRISIS IN THE COAL TRADE.—The miners who have been out on strike at Rowley Hall Colliery, Stafford- shire, for an increase of wages, resumed work on Friday morning at an advance of 10 per cent. The workmen numbered several hundreds. It is now considered that an advance of 10 per cent, will have to be paid at all collferie.s in order to prevent a general strike. A Con- ference of West Lancashire colliery proprietors on Friday decided to grant miners an advance of 10 per cent. THE EMPEROR WILLIAM. ROME, FRIDAY.—The Emperor William left Rome for Berlin this afternoon. REBELLION AT ZANZIBAR. , The Berlin Government have received a telegram from Zanzibar reporting a rebellion of the natives against the English Colony at Momba.s. Three English officials are reported killed, and many wounded. THE. EMPRESS FREDERICK AS A WITNESS. The "Star "hears from Berlin that it is the intention of the prosecution in the impending trial of Dr. Geffc- ken to put the Empress Frederick in the witness box. The late Emperor's diary was left in England at the time of the Jubilee, and it is supposed it was, then got at and copied. The Empress is to be examined on this point.
